solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tax advice about squalid dwelling

parts.note: cess is an old word for a tax or levy

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for advice is read backwards

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice

explanation.surface: Someone looking for guidance on what tax is owed on a run-down home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', but it is the reversal signal on the word for advice. Cess is an old word for a local tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A cesspit is figuratively any filthy, squalid place, so it serves as a grim kind of dwelling.

clue.text: Item left in car

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the letter goes within the car

parts.note: a coupe is a two-door car

explanation.surface: A single article was forgotten in the vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Item' looks like a thing, but it is the slang for a romantically linked pair.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is an informal term for two people in a relationship, a pair.

clue.text: Film — Fight Club — regularly shown during flipping day off?

parts.note: to spar is to fight, as boxers do in practice

indicators.note: shown during means appearing inside, so these letters go within the next piece
flipping means turning over, so the word for a day off is read backwards

parts.note: SAT is short for Saturday, a day off for many workers

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: The cult movie Fight Club is screened on a cursed holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fight Club' looks like the film title but is split apart. 'regularly' picks alternate letters of 'Club', 'flipping' reverses the day off, and 'shown during' puts the first inside the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartacus is the 1960 Kubrick epic about the gladiator who led a slave revolt against Rome.

clue.text: Help with venue for match at home

parts.note: a football or cricket match is played on a pitch
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: Assistance is needed with a ground for a home fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch in is an idiom for joining in and contributing effort to a shared task.

clue.text: Rent new flats, half of them at bottom of hill

indicators.note: at bottom of means placed below, so in this down clue these letters come after the hill

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, common on Dartmoor

indicators.note: half of them means only the first half of the word for flats is kept

parts.note: apartments are flats

explanation.surface: Letting out newly built apartments, half of which stand at the foot of a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of them' keeps the front half of the flats word; 'at bottom of' sets the rest below the hill in this down clue. 'Rent' is the past participle of rend, not the payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent is the past participle of rend, meaning torn or ripped into pieces.

clue.text: Olympic venue's head rejected Frenchman's late welcome?

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the whole string of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro hosted the 2016 Olympic Games; with the possessive it gives RIOS
nob is slang for the head

explanation.surface: The chief of the Olympic site turned away a Frenchman arriving late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses RIOS NOB, the whole of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The French greeting used in the evening translates as 'good evening', a welcome given late in the day.

clue.text: Oddly build seat on which to squat?

indicators.note: oddly means the letters in odd positions, first, third, fifth and so on, are taken

explanation.surface: A strangely constructed chair for crouching on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' takes the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters of 'build seat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bidet is a low basin one sits astride or crouches over to wash, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Collection of coins I found near a Mediterranean capital

indicators.note: a collection is a gathering up, so the letters of these words are brought together in a new order

explanation.surface: A coin hoard was discovered close to a city by the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collection of' looks like a hoard, but it is the anagram signal for COINS I, which gives NICOSI.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital city of Cyprus, an island in the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Where to see films on demand, except occasional Netflix premieres

indicators.note: premieres are first showings, so the first letter of each of these words is taken

explanation.surface: A cinema chain versus streaming, apart from the odd Netflix first showing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'premieres' takes the first letters of 'on demand except occasional Netflix'. 'On demand' looks like streaming jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: Odeon is a well-known chain of cinemas in Britain, and an odeon is a picture house generally.

clue.text: Fingering curious jewellery

parts.note: rum is a British informal word for odd or curious
bling is flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: Someone toying with an odd piece of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fingering' is not touching but informing on: in British slang to rumble someone is to find them out.
explanation.definitionFit: To finger someone is slang for identifying a culprit, just as rumbling means discovering their deception.

clue.text: NUT leader at sea, the same as before

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: The head of the teachers' union is out of his depth, but nothing has changed.
explanation.walkthrough: NUT is the National Union of Teachers, but here it is just three letters of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unchanged remains exactly as it previously was, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: The best comics needing no tips

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends, which are taken away here

parts.note: a very funny person is a scream, so comics are screams

explanation.surface: The finest comedians manage without gratuities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing no tips' removes the outer S and S from SCREAMS.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its finest part, as in 'the cream of the crop'.

clue.text: Apartment, not opening at the front? Check security device

indicators.note: not opening at the front means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: A flat whose door won't open at the front needs its lock looked at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not opening at the front' drops the F of FLAT, leaving LAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A latch is a simple fastening on a door or gate, a basic device for keeping it secure.

clue.text: Handmade herbal tea, briefly dipped in some salt water

indicators.note: dipped in means plunged inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: the Aral Sea is a salty inland lake in Central Asia, here just a body of salt water

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a tisane is an infusion of herbs

explanation.surface: Craft herbal tea is quickly dunked in brine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims TISANE to TISAN, which is 'dipped in' ARAL, the Central Asian sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Artisanal goods are made by skilled craftspeople, traditionally by hand rather than machine.

clue.text: Series about queen perhaps visiting a certain country

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: visiting means going into, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: one nation is a phrase for a single, united country
a queen is a female cat, so a cat is a queen perhaps

explanation.surface: A run of stories about a monarch, perhaps, touring a particular nation.
explanation.walkthrough: A queen is the term for a female cat, hence 'perhaps'. 'visiting' signals the insertion into the phrase for a single country.
explanation.definitionFit: A concatenation is a linked chain of things, so a series of connected events or items.

clue.text: Clear directions to enter old address

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: to enter means to go inside, so the directions are put within the word for address

parts.note: to orate is to address an audience in a speech
N and E are the compass directions north and east

explanation.surface: Clear instructions for getting into a former home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' is not a home but a verb, to speak to a crowd; 'to enter' signals the insertion of the two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to clear someone of blame or a charge.

clue.text: North Country inhabitant I badmouth audibly?

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the words are replaced by others that sound the same

parts.note: to badmouth is to slander, so I badmouth gives I slander

explanation.surface: A northern Englishman confesses to speaking ill of others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North Country' looks like the north of England; here it is a northern nation. 'I slander', said out loud, matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An Icelander is a native of Iceland, a nation in the far north of the Atlantic.

clue.text: Spirited swimming in turbulent waters

indicators.note: swimming means moving about freely, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lively swimmer braves rough seas.
explanation.definitionFit: Riptides are strong, rough currents in the sea that pull swimmers away from shore.

clue.text: Female enters cafe in Totnes after ordering drink

indicators.note: enters means goes inside, so this letter is placed within the other letters
after ordering means once rearranged, so the letters of these words are shuffled

explanation.surface: A woman walks into a cafe in a Devon town and orders a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after ordering' signals an anagram of CAFE IN TOTNES, and the F 'enters' it. Totnes is a market town in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: Instant coffee is a quick hot drink made from soluble granules or powder.

clue.text: First half of long track playing different genre of music?

indicators.note: playing means performing or fooling about, so the letters are rearranged
first half of means only the opening two letters of the word are kept

explanation.surface: Half of a long song is played in an unusual style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First half of' gives LO from 'long'; 'playing' rearranges LO and TRACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Alternative rock is a genre outside the mainstream, and 'alt' literally means alternative, or different.

clue.text: Socialists, fine Scottish lads?

parts.note: fab, short for fabulous, means fine or great
Ian is the Scottish form of John, a typical Scottish boy's name

explanation.surface: Political leftists who are also splendid young men from Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Fabian Society, the British group seeking gradual change toward a fairer society, are left-wing reformers.

clue.text: Sun has new leader, one complains

indicators.note: has new leader means the first letter of the word is replaced by a different one

parts.note: the sun is a shiner, something that shines

explanation.surface: The newspaper gets a new editor and a reader protests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun' looks like the newspaper, but it is the thing that shines. 'has new leader' swaps its S for W; the clue does not say which letter comes in, so crossings decide.
explanation.definitionFit: A whiner is someone who grumbles or moans persistently.

clue.text: List of office employees, perhaps, likely to obey siren?

parts.note: temps are temporary office staff; the singular serves as an adjective, as in a table of temps
a table is a list of figures or names

explanation.surface: A roster of workers who would follow a fire alarm, or a seductress.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'temp table' would be a list of temporary staff. A siren in Greek myth lured sailors to their doom, so the definition plays on alarms versus seductresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who can be tempted is easily lured, as by the seductive song of a siren.

clue.text: Dangerous creature, black, captured by degrees

indicators.note: captured by means held inside, so the letter goes within the degrees

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree, and two of them make degrees
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A deadly animal in black is caught by graduates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'degrees' gives two MAs, MAMA, and 'captured by' places B inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The mamba is a highly venomous African snake, notably the black mamba.

clue.text: Purchase includes dry sandwich

indicators.note: includes means holds within, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: to buy is to purchase
TT, teetotal, means dry, not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: A dry sandwich comes with the shopping.
explanation.walkthrough: BUTTY is northern British slang for a sandwich, as in a chip butty.
explanation.definitionFit: A butty is an informal word, chiefly from northern England, for a sandwich.

clue.text: Britain remains bold

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: The country still stands defiant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains' looks like a verb meaning stays; it is the noun, what is left after a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Brash means impudently self-assertive, a pushier sense of bold.

clue.text: Slow-witted type ultimately exasperated boss

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: an umbo is the raised boss at the centre of a shield

explanation.surface: A dim employee finally drives the manager up the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' is not a manager but the knob at the centre of a shield, the UMBO.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumbo is an informal, mildly insulting name for a stupid person.

clue.text: Trail round English forest leading to open-air eatery

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the first word goes about the letter

parts.note: to tag along is to trail behind, so tag means trail
the Forest of Arden is the woodland setting of As You Like It

explanation.surface: A path through a woodland brings walkers to an outdoor cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts TAG around E, giving TEAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea garden is an outdoor area where refreshments are served, a type of alfresco cafe.

clue.text: Lively scout crosses lake on sailing vessel

indicators.note: crosses means spans, so the first word is spread across the others, enclosing them

parts.note: a scout sent ahead to gather information is a spy

indicators.note: in an across clue, lake on vessel means the lake comes after it

parts.note: Noah's ark is a sailing vessel

explanation.surface: A sprightly boy scout on a boat trip across a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crosses' means the scout's word straddles the vessel and lake, and 'on' places the lake after the vessel, as usual in an across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparkly means vivacious and full of life, like someone with a sparkle.

clue.text: I'll guarantee critic has ignored opening chapter

indicators.note: has ignored means left out, so a letter is removed from the critic

parts.note: a censurer is someone who criticises

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A reviewer skipped the first chapter but promises it is good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has ignored' removes C, the 'opening' of 'chapter', from CENSURER. The definition is the answer speaking: one who guarantees.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensurer is one who makes certain of something, so it can say 'I will make sure'.
